ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_LI.I.mastery: Gives the meaning of idioms and fixed phrases (work like a dog, dog tired, burst into tears, a piece of cake, under the weather), completes them with the right word, and does not read them word for word, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_LI.C.mastery: Chooses the right word from the theme (employ, exploit, labour, wages, trafficking, abuse, rescue, protect) to complete a sentence, and does not mix a person with an action, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T1_PRONUNCIATION_AND_LI.M.mastery: Chooses the sentence or title that covers the whole text, tells it from a detail, and finds a specific detail asked for, in 8 of 10 new texts.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.REFE.mastery: Chooses the right reference for a need, puts words in alphabetical order beyond the first letter, and decides from guide words whether a word is on a page, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the book for a purpose
judge the relevance of a text
ENGL.G6.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING.SUIT.mastery: Chooses the book or text that fits a reader's purpose, level and interest (information, enjoyment, a topic), and does not choose by the cover, the length or the title alone, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T1_WORD_CLASSES.DETERMINE.mastery: Chooses some, enough, each or a lot of to fit the noun and the verb (each takes a singular noun and verb, a lot of takes plural or uncountable, some in an offer or a statement), and does not write each of the boys are or a lots of, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the entry for a field
choose the field a form needs
ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T1_GUIDED_WRITING.FORM_FI.mastery: Puts each detail in the field it belongs to (surname, date of birth, signature), follows the form's own instruction (block letters, tick one, write N/A), and says which fields a form needs for its purpose, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T2_PRONUNCIATION_AND_LI.P.mastery: Matches a proverb to its meaning, finishes it with the right word and picks the situation it fits, and does not read it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T2_PRONUNCIATION_AND_LI.S.mastery: Says that a simile compares with like or as and a metaphor says one thing is another, completes familiar similes (as hungry as a wolf), and does not write as ... like, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.STOR.mastery: Names the characters and the places in a short story, and puts four of its events in the order they happened, in 8 of 10 new passages.

forms: choose the clue that supports it
ENGL.G6.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.PRED.mastery: Uses clues in the story to choose the most likely next event and says which clue supports it, in 8 of 10 new passages.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.FACT.mastery: Finds an answer that is stated in the text, tells true from false and not stated, and does not pick a detail that sits near the answer, in 8 of 10 new passages.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.INFE.mastery: Works out what the text does not say outright (why a character acts, how they feel) and does not give an answer the text contradicts or merely repeats, in 8 of 10 new passages.

forms: choose the line that paints a picture
ENGL.G6.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.IMAG.mastery: Picks the words of a poem or story that make a picture, and says what the writer wants the reader to see, hear or feel, and does not pick the line that only gives a fact, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING.CHAR.mastery: Chooses the trait that the character's words and actions support (kind, selfish, brave, honest), and says which line is the evidence, and does not judge from the name or one word, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T2_WORD_CLASSES.CONCRETE_.mastery: Names nouns we can see or touch as concrete (mango, river) and nouns for ideas, feelings and qualities as abstract (honesty, hunger, bravery), and writes the noun form (honesty, not honest) in a gap, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: find the sentence that does not belong
ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T2_CREATIVE_WRITING.PARAG.mastery: Chooses the sentence that opens a paragraph, puts supporting sentences in a logical order and finds the sentence that does not belong, in 8 of 10 new paragraphs.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T3_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.mastery: Chooses the polite way to answer a call, to take a message, to interrupt (Excuse me, may I add something?) and to ask for clarification (Could you say that again, please?), and spots a rude or blunt turn, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T3_INTENSIVE_READING.CONT.mastery: Uses the words around an unfamiliar word, proverb or simile to choose its meaning and says which words gave the clue, in 8 of 10 new passages.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T3_CORRELATIVE_CONJUNCT.C.mastery: Pairs the two halves correctly (both with and, either with or, neither with nor, not only with but also), keeps the verb singular or plural to match, and writes no extra not after neither, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T3_CORRELATIVE_CONJUNCT.S.mastery: Writes the question word, then the subject, then the verb (Show me where the library is), without turning the verb round as in a question, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

forms: tell an acronym from an abbreviation
ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T3_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.A.mastery: Writes and reads the short form of common titles and words (Mr, Dr, etc.), expands Kenyan acronyms (KNEC, KWS, KRA), and tells an abbreviation from an acronym (an acronym is said as a word, like UNICEF), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T3_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.N.mastery: Spells numbers in words (forty, fourteen, ninety, eighth), writes ordinals with the right ending (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th), and does not begin a sentence with a figure, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T4_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.R.mastery: Chooses the right word (ambulance, paramedic, firefighter, siren, evacuate, first aid, emergency, rescue) for a rescue situation, and does not mix the person, the vehicle and the action, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES.RELATIVE_.mastery: Uses who for a person, which for a thing or animal, whose for belonging, and does not add a second pronoun (the boy who he won), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T4_WORD_CLASSES.INDEFINIT.mastery: Chooses some-, any-, no- or every- with -one, -body or -thing to fit the sentence, uses a singular verb with them, and does not write a double negative (did not see nobody) or noone, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the part or its place
ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T4_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.FOR.mastery: Tells where each part goes (address, date, greeting, subject line, closing, signature), matches the closing to the greeting (Dear Sir with Yours faithfully), and picks the polite formal wording, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T5_ADJECTIVES.ADJECTIVE_D.mastery: Tells the three forms apart and writes as ... as with the simple form, than with the comparative and the with the superlative, and does not write as taller as or the tallest than, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: pick the word with the same sound
ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T6_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.S.mastery: Picks the word with the same vowel sound as near (/ɪə/), tour (/ʊə/) or go (/əʊ/), or the word that starts with /f/, /v/ or an /h/ that is said (hour and honest start without it), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T6_PHRASAL_QUANTIFIERS.PH.mastery: Uses a number of and a good many with countable nouns, a great deal of and an amount of with uncountable nouns, and a piece, bottle, loaf or bar of for single items of an uncountable thing, with of every time, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T7_TENSE.FUTURE_CONTINUOU.mastery: Writes will be + verb-ing for an action that will be going on at a stated time (This time tomorrow we will be travelling), and does not write will travelling, will been or a present continuous, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.C.mastery: Puts the comma between items in a list, after an opening word or phrase, round extra information and before or after spoken words, and does not put one between subject and verb or use it to join two sentences, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T7_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.Q.mastery: Puts double quotation marks round the exact words spoken, closes them after the punctuation, keeps the capital letter at the start of the speech and the small letter after said in split speech, and does not use them for reported speech, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.R.mastery: Says that a riddle asks a puzzle with a hidden answer and a proverb gives advice or a truth, and answers a simple riddle by what it describes, not by the words in it, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T8_PRONUNCIATION_AND_VO.P.mastery: Chooses the phrasal verb and its particle for a meaning (give up, set off, break down, run out of, put up with, cope with, agree with, look after), and does not use the wrong preposition, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the passive of a sentence
ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T8_SENTENCE_PATTERNS.ACTI.mastery: Says whether the subject does the action (active) or receives it (passive), writes be + the past participle (The window was broken), matches be to the number, and does not leave out be or use the past tense in place of the participle, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T8_SENTENCE_PATTERNS.CONF.mastery: Chooses between each of these pairs from who is giving, who is receiving and which way the thing moves, and does not use one word for both as in Kiswahili, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T9_INTENSIVE_READING_FI.F.mastery: Says that a fact can be checked and an opinion says what someone thinks or feels (best, beautiful, should), and tells whether a short text is a made-up story or information, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: say what the adverb tells us
ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T9_ADVERBS.ADVERBS_USE.mastery: Tells what an adverb shows, uses well (not good), hard and hardly with their right meanings, puts the adverb of frequency before the main verb (always goes), and does not use an adjective after a verb of action, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T9_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.H.mastery: Writes the hyphen in compound words (well-known, mother-in-law), in numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine and in a compound before a noun (a ten-year-old boy, but ten years old), and does not write ten-years-old, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T10_CONJUNCTIONS.CONJUNCT.mastery: Chooses the conjunction that fits the meaning (contrast, condition, purpose, time), uses only one joining word (Although ... but ... is wrong), and does not write unless ... not, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T11_INTERROGATIVES.INTERR.mastery: Chooses the question word that fits the answer given (whose for owner, which for a choice from a set, how often for frequency, how long for time, how far for distance), in 8 of 10 new questions.

ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..mastery: Chooses a word with the same meaning (synonym) or the opposite meaning (antonym) in a sentence, and does not give a related word, the same word or the wrong kind of pair, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.READIN.T12_INTENSIVE_READING.POE.mastery: Finds the words that rhyme by sound (not by spelling), the line that repeats and the words a poem stresses, in 8 of 10 new poems.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T12_QUESTION_TAGS.QUESTIO.mastery: Adds the right tag to a statement: the same helper verb with the opposite sign and a pronoun (is/isn't, has/hasn't, does/doesn't, can/can't, will/won't), and writes aren't I after I am, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the part a journal has
ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T12_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING.JO.mastery: Names what a journal entry has (date, "I", the day's events in order, feelings) and what it does not (a greeting and a closing as in a letter, "Yours sincerely"), and tells a journal entry from a letter or a news report, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LISTEN.T13_PRONUNCIATION_AND_IN..mastery: Chooses the right word (profit, loss, import, export, customer, retailer, wholesaler, wages, budget) for a trading situation, and does not swap the opposite pairs, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.LANGUA.T13_WORD_CLASSES.PREPOSIT.mastery: Chooses between and among, since and for, during and for, by and with, and the preposition a word takes (interested in, afraid of, different from), and does not write interested on or afraid from, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G6.WRITIN.T13_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..mastery: Chooses the prefix (un-, dis-, mis-, re-, in-, im-) or suffix (-ful, -less, -ness, -ment, -able) that makes the meaning wanted, and keeps the spelling right (happy to happiness, care to careful), in 8 of 10 new items.

Spells words that often go wrong (receive, believe, separate, necessary, government, environment, tomorrow, library, February) from the sound, the rule or the picture of the word, in 8 of 10 new words.
